summary: Tetsuzo Tanikawa (1895–1989) worked in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Aichi Prefectural Zuiryo Senior High School, the First Higher School, and Kyoto University (~1916–1919), and held posts at Doshisha University (~1924–1931) and Hosei University (~1938–1965).

Teun Goudriaan is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. His career includes posts at Utrecht University, where he served as a committee member (attested 1989) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2000).

Thanissaro Bhikkhu (born 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Oberlin College (~1967–1971) and under Ajahn Fuang Jotiko (~1976–1986). He founded Metta Forest Monastery, serving as Abbot from 1993.
Thanon Chitkament works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Chitkament studied under guide Vishwas D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (both attested 2021).

Theodoor Paul Galestin (born 1907) specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Nicolaas Johannes Krom (~1931–1936) and served as a professor of South and Southeast Asian archaeology and ancient history at Leiden University in 1957.

Theodor Aufrecht (1822–1907) worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1842–1847), he held posts there (1850), at the Bodleian Library (1852), the University of Edinburgh (1861–1875), and the University of Bonn (1875–1889).

Theodor Benfey (1809–1881) was an Indologist and linguist. He completed his education, Ph.D., and habilitation at the University of Göttingen, where he spent his academic career as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881).

Theodor Bloch (1867–1909) specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch (~1888–1892) and continued his studies under Georg Bühler (~1894–1896).

Theodor Goldstücker (1821–1872) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Königsberg, Bonn, and under Peter von Bohlen, Karl Rosenkranz, Christian Lassen, and Eugène Burnouf. He held a Sanskrit professorship at University College London and the University of London.

Theodor Nöldeke (1836–1930) worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Göttingen, Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin under Benfey and Ewald, holding professorships at Göttingen, Kiel (1864–1872), and Strasbourg (1872–1906).

Theodor Zachariae (1851–1934) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Leipzig under Sauppe, Curtius, Brockhaus, and Benfey, habilitating at Greifswald. He held posts at Greifswald (1883) and Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).

Theodore Dwight Woolsey (1801–1889) worked in linguistics. He studied at Yale and Princeton, later serving as president of Yale University (1831–1871) and president of the American Oriental Society (~1863–1871).

Theodore Riccardi (1937–2023) worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Columbia University (attested 1974–1976 and 1990) and served as guest editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society (attested 1989).

Theodore Riccardi Jr. (born 1937) specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He served on the faculty at Columbia University, where he is attested as faculty in 2014 and Professor Emeritus in 2026.

Theodore Stcherbatsky (1866–1942) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi, and was a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1927–1931).
Theodorus Willem Juynboll (1866–1948) worked in religious studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1885–1893) and held a post at Utrecht University in 1916.
Theophil Gubler worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned a doctoral degree from the University of Basel in 1903, having studied under Jacob Wackernagel.
Thibaut d'Hubert works in the field of Indology. He has held posts at the University of Chicago and served as Vertretungsprofessor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Thich Nhat Hanh (1926–2022) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. Educated at Báo Quốc Temple, Saigon, Princeton, and Columbia, he held posts at Columbia, Princeton, Vạn Hạnh, and Cornell between 1961 and 1966.
Thich Thien Nghiem works in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor Shalini Singhal (attested 2012).
